docs.title: PN51 Homelab
docs.text:
Terraform creates four Ubuntu Server 26.04 LTS VMs on the PN51's Ubuntu Desktop KVM host. Ansible configures a one-server/three-worker K3s cluster, retained data disks, Prometheus, Grafana, Authelia MFA, Headlamp, Homepage, scoped Argo CD, and protected HTTPS ingress.

Start with provisioning. For an existing installation, use operations or monitoring.

Need Guide Build the lab from a prepared host Provisioning tutorial Understand ownership and failure modes Architecture Look up inputs, versions, and commands Reference Replace a worker or restore state Operations Keep a public repository safe Security Manage application GitOps without adopting infrastructure Argo CD ownership Check correctness and convergence Testing

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
The PN51 has 32 GiB RAM and a 1 TB NVMe disk. Four 4 GiB server VMs leave about half the memory for the Desktop host. Each VM has two vCPUs, a replaceable 64 GiB root disk, and a protected 64 GiB application data disk.

This is one physical failure domain. The control plane uses a single-member embedded etcd datastore for snapshots, not for high availability. Monitoring uses node-local persistent volumes by default. Back up both cluster state and application data outside this machine.

docs.title: Application GitOps
docs.text: Ansible installs Argo CD from the checksummed official Helm chart. It also owns Homepage, monitoring, authentication, TLS routes, network policy, and Argo CD's bootstrap projects. Argo CD is for reviewed application workloads, not a second reconciler for the infrastructure that installed it.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
Owner Resources Terraform Host-side VM network, identities, root/data disks, and cloud-init Ansible and Helm Host/guest baseline, K3s, monitoring, Homepage, Authelia, Headlamp, Argo CD bootstrap and ingress Argo CD applications Reviewed namespaced workloads in fitness-tracker only

The default project allows no repositories or destinations. The homelab project permits only https://github.com/TheNewThinkTank/homelab.git and the fitness-tracker namespace on this cluster. It cannot manage cluster-scoped resources or the platform, monitoring, argocd, or kube-system namespaces. Ansible precreates the application namespace with restricted Pod Security.

Argo CD itself remains a privileged cluster controller: protect its namespace, administrator account, repository credentials, and project administration. Project limits are not isolation from a compromised controller.

docs.title: Access and Authentication
docs.text:
Open https://argocd.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io or use the Homepage link. Authelia MFA protects the external route; Argo CD then requires its own login. Anonymous Argo CD access is disabled and the default authenticated role is read-only. The initial admin credential is a Kubernetes Secret, not a public Helm value or an Ansible Vault field. Follow Argo CD access to retrieve it in your own terminal and rotate it after first use.

Traefik terminates HTTPS. The Argo CD server listens on HTTP only inside its private namespace, behind a default-deny policy and the reviewed ingress rule. This does not disable Kubernetes API certificate verification.

docs.title: Application Example
docs.text:
The bootstrap does not create an Application, enable application auto-sync, or adopt existing infrastructure. The existing pn51/application.yaml example now selects the homelab project. Review it before applying: it follows HEAD and its explicit automated sync, self-heal, and prune settings will take effect if you choose to install it.

The example's application Secret has empty values and is not a production secret source. Use a dedicated encrypted-secret or external-secret workflow for real credentials; base64 is not protection. Validate images, manifests, application backups, and any ingress/authentication changes before enabling reconciliation. Changes in this local checkout are not available to Argo CD until deliberately published to the configured Git repository.

To admit a different repository or namespace, review the project template and the corresponding Ansible group variables; do not casually widen the project to *. Do not edit Ansible-owned bootstrap resources through an Application.

Run make argocd-chart-check, make configure, make verify, and make idempotence after changing the bootstrap. Chart upgrades can change CRDs; Helm rollback does not restore application data or reverse CRD migrations.

See security, architecture, and operations.

docs.title: How to Use Platform Services
docs.text: The Ansible monitoring role installs a SHA-256-pinned kube-prometheus-stack archive. It includes Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, dashboards, rules, and Prometheus Operator CRDs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Complete provisioning. Use the private administrator kubeconfig on a trusted controller and keep make tunnel running. Services are private; the guarded cutover adds LAN-only HTTPS access, not internet exposure.

docs.title: HTTPS and Authelia
docs.text:
After make cutover CONFIRM=retire-host-k3s, the default URLs are:

Service URL Authelia https://auth.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Homepage https://homepage.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Argo CD https://argocd.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Grafana https://grafana.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Prometheus https://prometheus.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Alertmanager https://alertmanager.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io Headlamp https://headlamp.pn51.192.168.1.20.sslip.io

Authelia's generated gus credential is in the encrypted vault. Retrieve it only through your trusted terminal/password-manager workflow. MFA enrollment uses the private filesystem notifier under Authelia's /data/notifications.txt; read enrollment codes only in your own terminal, never in chat or public logs.

The internal CA is .local/pki/ca.crt. Nothing installs it into the Mac's trust store. Browser trust remains an explicit operator decision; do not disable TLS validation in provisioning. Router DNS-rebinding protection can block sslip.io answers; a deliberately configured private DNS domain is an alternative.

docs.title: Homepage
docs.text: Homepage is the default landing page after an Authelia login without a specific return URL. It links the platform and monitoring services, including Argo CD. Its settings and service cards are declared in the platform role's Homepage template; edits are applied by make configure with a checksum-driven rollout. It has no Kubernetes token, Docker socket, API credentials, or persistent state. Writable cache/log files are disposable; configuration is reconstructed from Git.

docs.title: Argo CD Access
docs.text:
After Authelia MFA, Argo CD requires a separate login. On first installation, retrieve its generated admin password only in your own trusted terminal:

kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n argocd get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode

Do not post the password in chat, logs, or Git. Change it in Argo CD after first use, retain the replacement in your password manager, and remove the bootstrap Secret once no longer needed. Its absence after rotation is normal.

The homelab project is restricted to the reviewed repository and fitness-tracker namespace. No application is deployed or auto-synced by bootstrap. See GitOps ownership and the application example.

docs.title: Headlamp Access
docs.text:
In your own terminal, use the private lab kubeconfig to mint a read-only token:

kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n platform create token headlamp-viewer --duration=1h

Enter it in Headlamp after Authelia MFA. Do not post the token in chat or store it in Git. The default role cannot read Secrets or mutate cluster resources. Cluster-admin access is not granted by the bootstrap.

docs.title: How to Open Grafana
docs.text:
In a dedicated terminal:

kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n monitoring port-forward \
    --address 127.0.0.1 service/monitoring-grafana 3000:80

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000. The default username is admin; the generated password is in the encrypted vault. Retrieve it through your trusted local vault workflow, not a public terminal transcript or chat. Do not bind forwarding to 0.0.0.0.

Dashboards supplied by the chart are available immediately. Grafana's data and customizations persist on its 2 GiB PVC. Its admin password is initialized in the database; changing only the bootstrap Secret does not rotate an existing account.

docs.title: How to Open Prometheus or Alertmanager
docs.text:
Use separate terminals as needed:

kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n monitoring port-forward \
    --address 127.0.0.1 service/monitoring-prometheus 9090:9090

kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n monitoring port-forward \
    --address 127.0.0.1 service/monitoring-alertmanager 9093:9093

Open http://127.0.0.1:9090 or http://127.0.0.1:9093. These services have no independent authentication boundary when bypassing ingress with administrator port forwarding and must stay private. The LAN HTTPS routes require Authelia. Stop each forward with Ctrl-C when finished.

Prometheus retains up to three days or about 8 GB in a 12 GiB PVC. Its WAL and compaction need space beyond the retention-size setting. Alertmanager uses 1 GiB for silences and notification state. No alert email/webhook destination is invented; configure a receiver and its credentials deliberately when required.

docs.title: How to Check Health
docs.text:
make verify
kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n monitoring get pods,pvc,services
kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig -n monitoring get prometheus,alertmanager

Expect private ClusterIP services, three Bound persistent claims, ready operator and exporters, and ready Prometheus/Alertmanager instances. Inspect Prometheus Status > Targets when a scrape fails. The workflow disables etcd, controller-manager, scheduler, and kube-proxy monitors/rules that do not map to this default K3s installation; it does not open their bind addresses just to make dashboards green.

Node-exporter inspects the host but uses pod networking rather than a host metrics listener. The monitoring namespace explicitly permits privileged pod security for host inspection; do not admit unrelated or untrusted workloads.

docs.title: How to Change Retention or Storage
docs.text:
Edit the non-secret monitoring values and run make chart-check, then make configure and make verify. Review the resource reference before increasing requests or retention on this 32 GiB host.

To use external storage, install and validate that storage class separately and set the Ansible variable monitoring_storage_class. Changing the variable does not migrate an existing PVC. Back up and restore data through a planned storage migration; PVC storage class and many volume fields are immutable.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check Prometheus/Alertmanager Pending PVC binding, worker scheduling, local-path helper pod events, memory and disk Grafana unavailable after restart Its Deployment, bound PVC, node affinity, database health, and permissions Targets down Endpoint discovery, kubelet TLS/authentication, CNI traffic, and VM firewall state Chart checksum mismatch Stop; verify the reviewed version/hash pair and inspect the cached archive CRD conflict on upgrade Review upstream migrations and current field ownership; do not force conflicts blindly Data unavailable after VM replacement Check the retained data disk mount and original node name; restore from off-host backup if hardware failed Old Grafana password still works Existing database password is separate from the bootstrap Secret

See backup and recovery, security, and live acceptance.

docs.title: How to Operate and Rebuild the Lab
docs.text: These procedures assume the provisioning tutorial has completed and the live acceptance checks pass. Keep an independent controller and off-host backups; the PN51 must not be its own only recovery environment.

docs.title: How to Reconcile Desired State
docs.text:
make plan
make configure
make verify

Apply Terraform only when the reviewed plan contains intended VM changes. A normal Ansible run repairs declared package/file/service state without rebooting or unconditionally upgrading everything. If you changed Terraform networking, regenerate inventory and inspect connectivity before configuring guests.

Do not change node names, pod/service CIDRs, or the server token in a running cluster as routine configuration. These values are cluster identity, not casual tuning knobs.

docs.title: How to Replace a Worker
docs.text:
1. Check backups and identify the generated worker name with kubectl --kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig get nodes -o wide.
  2. Run make replace-worker NODE=pn51-worker-2.
  3. Inspect the saved Terraform plan. The helper rejects changes outside that worker's domain, root disk, and seed. Protected data disks are not allowed to change. Type the exact confirmation only when destroying its root disk is intended.
  4. Run make trust-guest-keys. The guest agent supplies the new public key through the already trusted PN51 libvirt connection; only the private repo-local guest host-key file is updated.
  5. Run make configure, make verify, and make idempotence.

The helper requires the server and remaining workers to be Ready. It refuses unprotected or uncertain local persistent volumes before draining. Volumes under /srv/homelab-data/storage on the selected node survive on its unchanged data disk. It respects pod disruption budgets and does not use forced eviction. EmptyDir data is explicitly disposable and is deleted by drain.

After a successful Terraform replacement, it deletes the old Kubernetes Node and waits for K3s to remove the corresponding node-password Secret. The new guest can then rejoin with the same stable node name. Never manually erase an active worker's identity just to make a join succeed.

Approved automation can supply CONFIRM_REPLACEMENT='replace pn51-worker-2' with the Make command. The phrase must match the selected worker exactly; node health, protected-volume, complete-plan, and control-plane refusal checks still run. Without this option, the interactive confirmation remains mandatory.

The live recovery exercise replaced pn51-worker-2 and its root disk, then reverified SSH identity and reapplied Ansible. A probe on its retained data disk kept the same SHA-256, Alertmanager kept its original Bound PVC, and all live acceptance checks passed afterward. The temporary probe was removed. This does not establish whole-host disaster recovery or etcd snapshot restore.

docs.title: Data-Bearing Workers
docs.text:
The default local-path provisioner stores data under /srv/homelab-data/storage on one VM's protected data disk. A persistent volume's node affinity prevents it from following a pod to a different worker. Kubernetes rescheduling is not a storage migration.

Protected data disks remain attached after root replacement, and the same node name restores volume affinity. This does not move data to a different node or protect against physical disk failure. For unprotected data, first use a workload-specific backup/restore or migrate to an existing off-host storage class. Verify restored data, remove obsolete claims/PVs only when their contents are no longer needed, and rerun the guarded procedure. Do not remove affinity or delete PVs merely to bypass its warning.

docs.title: How to Update Software
docs.text:
Take and verify backups first. Update one ownership layer at a time:

Layer Procedure Controller dependencies Review project changes, run uv lock, commit lockfile, run make setup check Provider Review release notes and planned replacements; update provider pin and lockfile; run mock tests Ubuntu base image Choose a dated official image, verify signed checksums, update URL/hash, review replacement plan Ubuntu guest packages Use a drained, one-at-a-time maintenance window for upgrades and required reboots K3s Review supported upgrade path and release checksum, change version/hash together, run offline and live tests Monitoring Review chart/Grafana/operator upgrade notes, update version/hash together, render/check CRD changes

K3s server changes happen before workers. The single API server can be unavailable during restart; workers are processed one at a time and drained only when their K3s binary/config/unit changes. Existing disruption budgets can legitimately stop an upgrade. Never bypass them without understanding the affected workload.

Guest security updates run unattended, but automatic reboots are disabled. During maintenance, drain the selected worker, upgrade packages, reboot if required, wait for Ready, uncordon, and verify workloads before moving to the next. A server reboot is a planned API outage. Server packages are not frozen by the cloud-image pin; current security packages come from Ubuntu's repositories.

The role reconciles chart CRDs separately with server-side apply. Conflicts are not force-overwritten. Helm's atomic rollback does not roll back CRDs, databases, or PVC data; follow upstream migration requirements and keep backups.

docs.title: How to Back Up
docs.text:
Back up these independent layers:

Layer Required off-host material Terraform State and backup, private tfvars/backend configuration, provider lockfile Controller Encrypted vault, separate vault password, SSH key recovery, trusted CA details K3s etcd snapshot plus the original server token and configuration Applications Database-native backups and persistent volume contents Hypervisor Ansible host configuration, Terraform state, and cold libvirt disk backups to independent storage

K3s takes a local embedded-etcd snapshot every six hours and retains 14. Those snapshots are stored on the protected server data disk, but still need off-host export. Create a manual snapshot through the verified server SSH connection before a change:

sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s etcd-snapshot save --name before-maintenance
sudo /usr/local/bin/k3s etcd-snapshot ls

These are guest commands, not controller commands. Export snapshots from /srv/homelab-data/etcd-snapshots to encrypted storage on another machine. Protect the original token with them; losing it can make a snapshot unusable. Configure K3s S3 snapshot support separately if you want automatic off-host exports. This repository does not invent an S3 endpoint or silently claim off-host backup automation.

An etcd snapshot contains Kubernetes objects, not Grafana's SQLite database, Prometheus's TSDB, or arbitrary PV files. Quiesce or use each application's documented backup mechanism. Stop the relevant VMs before copying their qcow2 files; copying running qcow2 disks is not a consistent backup. Test restoration with isolated libvirt names and a non-conflicting network.

docs.title: How to Recover the Control Plane
docs.text:
The automated worker helper refuses the server. Server replacement needs the original vault/token, the relevant etcd snapshot, preserved addressing, and a separate restore window.

  1. Stop the old server permanently and prevent it from coming back with the same address. Preserve its disk for investigation if possible.
  2. Restore a tested cold libvirt backup, or provision a fresh Ubuntu 26.04 guest at the declared identity. Verify its SSH fingerprint. Do not blindly run normal configuration against an empty datastore: that would create a new cluster.
  3. Install the same pinned K3s version and baseline. Securely restore the original root token/config files and place the snapshot on the guest.
  4. Follow the upstream single-server snapshot restore procedure. With K3s stopped, use its explicit server --cluster-reset --cluster-reset-restore-path=/absolute/snapshot/path operation, the original token, and the original configuration. This is a manual recovery action, not a normal service flag; do not leave cluster-reset in the systemd unit.
  5. Start K3s normally. Verify restored node identities and resources before reconciling anything. Existing workers should connect to the restored API; investigate identities rather than deleting them blindly.
  6. Export a fresh administrator kubeconfig, reconcile desired state, restore PV data as needed, then run make verify and make idempotence.

Keep recovery instructions matched to the pinned release and test them in an isolated lab. A full restore has not been proven merely because an offline unit test passes.

docs.title: How to Rebuild Everything
docs.text: Take off-host backups and verify recoverability. make destroy requests a full Terraform removal, but retained data disks deliberately prevent that plan from being applied. Local ignored files are not automatically erased. Review the full destroy plan before confirming. The protected data disks have prevent_destroy and deliberately block a full destroy. Deleting retained application data needs a separate, reviewed change to that protection after backup and recovery checks.

docs.title: Legacy Cutover and Rollback
docs.text:
Keep the API tunnel running and pass make verify before:

make cutover CONFIRM=retire-host-k3s

The playbook cold-stops the old host cluster using its installed K3s killall helper, archives its datastore, token, configuration, and default local-path storage under /var/backups/homelab/legacy-k3s, and fetches a SHA-256-verified copy into .local/backups/legacy-k3s on the controller. It does not import old application data into the new cluster or uninstall the old host files.

The live cutover completed: the old host service is stopped and disabled, the private off-host archive checksum matches, all four VMs remain running, and the least-privilege ingress proxy is enabled. LAN HTTPS checks validated the lab CA; Authelia returned 200 and anonymous requests to each dashboard redirected to it. The archive and original host files remain recovery material, not stale active infrastructure.

If publishing ingress fails, the old files remain available. From the PN51 root terminal, stop homelab-ingress and run systemctl enable --now k3s to restore the preserved legacy service. Do not run both host ingress services on the same ports. Keep the archive until data restoration and the new service access have been tested.

For an intentionally empty new cluster, apply again, verify new SSH fingerprints, and configure from the preserved private inputs. For recovery, restore etcd and application data instead of allowing a fresh cluster to replace the old one. Never discard Terraform state while the corresponding resources still exist: restore the state or import the exact existing resources first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Failure Safe response Drain blocked Inspect disruption budgets and replica health; do not force eviction by default Replacement stops after VM apply Inspect saved plan/state and new VM; finish verified identity cleanup and provisioning Replacement blocked by PV Migrate or restore its data before deleting its VM Node remains cordoned after interruption Confirm node health, then explicitly uncordon it API lost after server rebuild Restore the original datastore/token; do not join workers to an unintended new cluster Helm upgrade rollback fails Inspect CRD and data migrations separately from release rollback

See security, reference, and live acceptance.

docs.title: Build the Four-VM Lab
docs.text:
Keep Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 LTS on the PN51. Terraform creates four Ubuntu Server VMs on native KVM/libvirt; Ansible configures K3s, retained storage, monitoring, Authelia, Headlamp, and protected HTTPS ingress.

All Make commands below run from this repository on the Mac controller. A PN51 root shell is not the controller and does not contain this Makefile. No Mac packages, shell files, routes, DNS settings, or trust-store changes are made. Generated controller files stay under this repo's ignored .local directory.

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
• PN51 with 32 GiB RAM, sufficient free NVMe capacity, AMD virtualization enabled, and a working ssh pn51 alias with an already verified host key.
  • Ubuntu host sudo authentication supplied directly in a terminal. Ubuntu 26.04 uses sudo-rs; do not add unsupported timestamp_type settings or passwordless host sudo just to automate setup.
  • Existing Terraform 1.10+, uv, Helm 3, a compatible kubectl, OpenSSH, Git, and Make on the controller. No Homebrew or global Mac installation is part of this workflow.
  • An existing PN51 SSH key; only its public half enters Terraform/cloud-init.
  • A non-overlapping private subnet. The default 10.51.0.0/24 NAT network works over the PN51's existing Wi-Fi without replacing its LAN connection.

The live audit found Ubuntu 26.04.1, a Ryzen 7 5700U, about 31 GiB usable RAM, and Wi-Fi address 192.168.1.20. Reserve that address on the router or update the SSH alias and lab_domain deliberately. No router configuration is changed automatically.

docs.title: Step 1: Prepare Local Tools and Private Inputs
docs.text:
make setup
make init-local
make check

init-local discovers the existing SSH public key, writes private Terraform inputs, generates an encrypted vault and private vault-password file, and creates an internal CA/certificate. It reuses existing credentials and PKI instead of silently regenerating cluster identity. The ISO helper and Python dependencies are installed only in the repo's virtual environment.

The vault password, private TLS keys, kubeconfig, and state are sensitive even though Git ignores them. Back them up securely and store the vault password separately in a password manager. TLS downloads use verified system trust and pinned SHA-256 checks; never use insecure TLS flags.

docs.title: Step 2: Reconcile the Ubuntu Host
docs.text:
make host

Enter the PN51 password at BECOME password: in the local task terminal, never in chat. This installs KVM/libvirt and cloud-image tools, grants gus access to system libvirt, allows guest NAT egress through UFW, and prevents host suspend. It does not reinstall Ubuntu or stop the existing host-native K3s cluster. New SSH sessions pick up the libvirt group membership.

The VM storage directory is owned by QEMU and the privileged libvirt group with mode 0750; unrelated host users cannot read the guest disks. Reconcile the host role before storing cluster credentials.

The host role selects qemu-system-x86 explicitly. Ubuntu 26.04's qemu-kvm is a virtual package with multiple providers, not an installable candidate.

Host automation explicitly uses the already installed /usr/bin/sudo.ws. Ubuntu's sudo-rs wraps custom prompts, which Ansible 2.20 does not recognize; this otherwise times out during fact gathering. The override is only in the host inventory, does not change sudo policy or the default executable, and does not affect guest passwordless sudo.

docs.title: Step 3: Plan and Create Four VMs
docs.text:
make plan
make apply

The plan should contain only this lab's pool, NAT network, pinned image, four cloud-init seeds, four root disks, four protected data disks, and four domains. Each guest gets two vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM, leaving about half the host's RAM for Ubuntu Desktop. Root and data disks are sparse 64 GiB qcow2 volumes.

Terraform confirmation is retained. Do not apply unexpected deletions or control-plane replacement. prevent_destroy on data disks deliberately blocks a full destroy; it is not a substitute for off-host backups.

The domain transform declares concrete disk file paths and the qcow2 backing chain so libvirt can apply its security labeling. The repo-local ISO helper emits the pinned provider's legacy primary filenames as well as the normal guest filenames. Guest link-local addresses remain computed observations; cloud-init owns the declared static IPv4 addresses.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Guest Identity and Open the API Tunnel
docs.text:
make trust-guest-keys

The helper reads public guest SSH keys through the authenticated PN51 libvirt guest agent, checks declared MAC identities, and writes .local/known_hosts. It does not trust unauthenticated keyscan output or change the Mac's global known-hosts file. Cloud-init supplies key-only SSH and passwordless guest sudo to the protected ubuntu automation account.

In another local terminal, keep this running:

make tunnel

The Kubernetes API is forwarded only to 127.0.0.1:16443. No controller route or global kubeconfig is changed. Keep the tunnel open for configure, verification, Helm operations, and worker replacement.

The tunnel sends SSH keepalives every 30 seconds. If the SSH connection exits after a network interruption, restart make tunnel before using the private API.

docs.title: Step 5: Configure the Cluster and Add-ons
docs.text:
make configure
make verify
make idempotence

Ansible waits for cloud-init, checks that targets are Ubuntu server VMs, mounts the retained data disks, hardens SSH/kernel settings, and installs K3s. Workers join serially with a CA-pinned token. Monitoring and Authelia use the dedicated homelab-retained storage class under /srv/homelab-data/storage.

The controller reconciles Prometheus CRDs, vaulted Secrets, the pinned monitoring chart, the pinned Argo CD bootstrap, Homepage, Authelia, Headlamp, ingress, and network policies. Argo CD receives no Application automatically and its project is limited to the reviewed repository and application namespace. Secret values are not stored in Terraform or Helm values. verify checks four Ready nodes, versions, workload health, retained PVCs, scrape targets, and essential system add-ons. idempotence requires a full second guest run with zero changes or hidden failures.

Homepage is the authenticated service landing page. Argo CD retains its own administrator login behind Authelia MFA; retrieve its initial credential only through the documented trusted-terminal workflow. Review GitOps ownership before enabling an Application.

docs.title: Optional Guest Dotfiles
docs.text:
Guest dotfiles remain opt-in and come from the pinned public sibling project's published commit, never copied controller files or mutable branches:

make configure CONFIG_FILE=.local/config.yml
make idempotence CONFIG_FILE=.local/config.yml

Review pn51/ansible/config.example.yml before preparing the private config. This role installs only the lightweight guest package set and user environment; it does not configure the Mac. Use the same config file for both reconciliation and idempotence.

docs.title: Step 6: Retire the Legacy Host Cluster and Publish Ingress
docs.text:
make cutover CONFIRM=retire-host-k3s

This first runs live cluster checks, cold-archives the old host cluster, verifies an off-host copy under .local/backups/legacy-k3s, then enables HAProxy forwarding to the VM ingress. The legacy files remain for rollback. Old application data is preserved in the archive, not silently imported or discarded.

Read legacy cutover and rollback before confirming. Review any non-default old PV storage separately. After cutover, use the service access guide to enroll Authelia MFA and obtain a short-lived, read-only Headlamp token in your own terminal.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Action No rule for make host Run from this repo on the Mac, not the PN51 root shell Remote libvirt socket unavailable Complete make host, then open a fresh SSH session for group membership Unknown guest SSH key Run make trust-guest-keys; never disable host-key checking API endpoint unavailable Keep make tunnel running and check local port 16443 Cloud-init fails or apt is locked Inspect cloud-init status --long and its logs; do not delete apt lockfiles Token mismatch Restore the original vault; do not invent a new token for the old datastore PVC stays Pending Check the retained storage class, protected disk mount, node affinity, and pod events Browser certificate warning The internal CA is not installed into the Mac trust store automatically

Offline checks validate declarations, not a completed live migration. Only live verification, repeated convergence, and tested data recovery establish that the PN51 is rebuildable.

docs.title: Configuration and Command Reference
docs.text: Run commands from the repository root. Relative inventory, role, collection, and local-artifact paths depend on that working directory.

docs.title: Versions and Artifacts
docs.text:
Component Pin or supported range Location Host Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 LTS Ansible-managed KVM/libvirt Terraform >= 1.10, < 2; CI uses 1.16.6 Terraform required-version constraint libvirt provider dmacvicar/libvirt 0.8.3 Terraform versions and provider lockfile Ubuntu base 26.04 amd64, build 20260927 Terraform image URL and SHA-256 Guests Ubuntu Server, no desktop installation Cloud-init and guest baseline role K3s v1.37.1+k3s1 Ansible group variables; binary SHA-256 Helm 3.x; CI uses 3.22.1 Local CLI and CI setup Monitoring chart 92.9.0 Ansible group variables; archive SHA-256 Authelia 4.39.15 Ansible group variables Headlamp v0.35.0 Ansible group variables Homepage v2.7.0 Ansible group variables; declarative platform config Argo CD Chart 10.11.7, app v3.5.7 Official chart SHA-256 pin; Ansible bootstrap role Python 3.13 or 3.14; CI uses 3.13 Project constraint and uv.lock Ansible Core 2.20.6 Project dependencies and uv.lock Collections ansible.posix 2.1.0, kubernetes.core 6.1.0 Ansible requirements

Image and binary pins are immutable inputs, not permission to ignore security updates. Ubuntu's package repositories evolve; package installation is convergent, not a bit-for-bit image build. Review and update version/checksum pairs together, commit lockfiles, then run all tests and the live gates.

docs.title: Terraform Inputs
docs.text:
make init-local writes ignored .local/terraform.tfvars.json using the existing PN51 SSH public key. Make passes that file explicitly. The committed example documents overrides and deliberately contains no real key.

Input Type Default Constraint or behavior libvirt_uri string qemu+ssh://gus@pn51/system Remote system libvirt over the existing SSH identity host_ssh_alias string pn51 Verified jump-host alias network_cidr string 10.51.0.0/24 Dedicated canonical IPv4 NAT /24 gateway string 10.51.0.1 Subnet's first usable address ssh_public_keys list(string) required OpenSSH public keys, not paths or private keys cluster_name string pn51 2-32 lowercase DNS-safe characters node_ip_offset number 40 Four usable consecutive addresses, excluding gateway dns_servers list(string) 1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9 At least one reachable IPv4 resolver vm_memory_mb number 4096 Integer 4096-6144; retain host RAM vm_vcpus number 2 Integer 2-4 per guest vm_disk_gb number 64 Sparse replaceable root disk, at least 32 GiB vm_data_disk_gb number 64 Protected retained data disk, at least 32 GiB image_path / image_checksum nullable strings pinned manifest Reviewed local path and SHA-256 overrides pod_cidr string 10.42.0.0/16 IPv4 prefix at most /22; immutable on a running cluster service_cidr string 10.43.0.0/16 IPv4 prefix at most /24; immutable on a running cluster

The node, pod, and service networks must not overlap. Check router, VPN, and remote-site networks too: Terraform cannot discover your external routing table. The private libvirt network supplies deterministic MACs and guest addresses; it does not reserve addresses on the physical LAN or change the Wi-Fi interface.

Changing the cluster name, network identity, imported base image, or disk inputs can be destructive or require an explicit rebuild. Always inspect the plan.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: nodes maps stable names to MACs, roles, and addresses. ansible_inventory contains one k3s_server, three k3s_agents, SSH username, guest Python path, cluster CIDRs, and the service subnet's host-10 DNS address. Neither output contains passwords, private keys, Kubernetes tokens, or kubeconfig data.

docs.title: Controller Environment
docs.text:
Variable Purpose UV_CACHE_DIR, ANSIBLE_HOME, TMPDIR Make keeps generated state inside .local HELM_CONFIG_HOME, HELM_CACHE_HOME, HELM_DATA_HOME Repo-local Helm state ANSIBLE_CONFIG Normally unset; the root configuration is selected automatically ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE Optional absolute path outside Git; mode 0600 SSL_CERT_FILE Optional verified CA bundle for Python tooling behind a private CA UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=true Use system trust when installing controller tools behind a private CA

Never set provider insecure mode, disable SSH host checks, or turn off Kubernetes TLS validation to get past a trust failure. Install the correct CA or verify the host fingerprint instead.

docs.title: Vault Schema
docs.text:
make vault generates and encrypts these fields without writing plaintext:

Key Requirement k3s_token 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; preserve the original for restore grafana_admin_password At least 24 characters; generated value is longer authelia_password Generated bootstrap password; retrieve only through a trusted terminal authelia_password_hash Argon2id hash for the file-backed administrator authelia_session_secret Random 64-character hex session key authelia_storage_key Random 64-character hex storage encryption key authelia_jwt_secret Random 64-character hex identity-validation key

Guest passwords remain locked. Grafana's secret is a bootstrap credential: changing it does not reset an already-initialized Grafana database.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Effect Live resources? make setup Install frozen Python dependencies and pinned local collections No make init-local Prepare private Terraform inputs, encrypted vault, vault password, internal PKI No make host Reconcile Ubuntu KVM/libvirt, NAT egress, and host suspend policy Yes; remote sudo prompt make image Download and SHA-256-verify the pinned cloud image No make init Initialize Terraform provider/backend No mutation of VMs make plan Refresh and preview VM changes Reads remote libvirt make apply Apply after Terraform confirmation Yes make inventory Validate Terraform outputs and write private JSON inventory Reads state make vault Prompt for vault password and create encrypted credentials No make trust-guest-keys Read verified public guest SSH keys into .local/known_hosts Reads libvirt guest agents make tunnel Keep API forwarded to localhost:16443 No cluster mutation make configure Reconcile server guests, K3s, monitoring, Homepage, Argo CD bootstrap, authentication, and ingress Yes make cutover CONFIRM=retire-host-k3s Cold legacy backup, verified off-host copy, owned LAN ingress proxy Yes; guarded legacy outage make kube-shell Open a controller shell with this lab's kubeconfig selected No mutation of cluster resources make verify Check nodes, versions, workloads, PVCs, health, scrape targets, Helm test Read checks plus temporary Helm test pod make idempotence Apply once, then require zero changes on a full second run Yes make replace-worker NODE=pn51-worker-2 Plan, guard, confirm, drain, and replace only that worker Yes; destroys its root disk make destroy Plan full destruction; protected data disks block it Requires separate reviewed removal of protection make lint Terraform formatting, Ruff, and production Ansible lint No make chart-check Verify checksum, lint/render real chart, parse CRDs No make argocd-chart-check Verify official chart checksum, three CRDs, private access, and application-project scope No make test-templates Render actual Ansible templates twice for four fake guests No make platform-check Render and validate MFA, TLS, restricted pods, RBAC, and network policies No make test Mocked Terraform, chart, template, and Python tests No make check Lint, tests, and strict documentation build No make secrets-scan Redacted Gitleaks scan of Git history No make docs / make docs-serve Build / preview documentation No

VAULT_FILE defaults to .local/vault.yml. VAULT_ARGS defaults to --vault-password-file .local/vault-password; an operator-managed password can use make configure VAULT_ARGS='--vault-password-file /absolute/private/path'. CONFIG_FILE is unset by default; set it to .local/config.yml for optional non-secret Ansible settings. Both configuration and idempotence runs use the same file. Secret values still belong in the encrypted vault, not Make arguments. UV can select a different uv executable. Do not put secret values in Make arguments or extra-vars strings.

docs.title: GitOps Bootstrap Settings
docs.text:
Variable Default Contract homepage_image ghcr.io/gethomepage/homepage:v2.7.0 Version-pinned, credential-free service dashboard argocd_chart_version 10.11.7 Update together with its reviewed SHA-256 argocd_namespace argocd Trusted bootstrap/controller namespace argocd_application_namespace fitness-tracker Only admitted application destination argocd_application_repository Public TheNewThinkTank homelab HTTPS Git URL Only admitted application source; no embedded credentials

Argo CD's initial administrator password is generated in Kubernetes and is not an Ansible Vault field. Its bootstrap, CRDs, projects, and ingress remain Ansible/Helm-owned. See GitOps ownership and service access before enabling application sync.

docs.title: Optional Dotfiles
docs.text:
The sibling dotfiles repository owns user configuration and its node package manifest. Homelab fetches a pinned public commit and delegates configuration to that repository; it does not copy workstation dotfiles or private overrides.

Variable Default Contract dotfiles_enabled false Enable explicitly through your private configuration dotfiles_repository Public TheNewThinkTank dotfiles HTTPS Git URL Credential-free GitHub URL dotfiles_revision b703d09fe26c5bd7e9daac92450f3c313a4c7c6a Reviewed full lowercase 40-character published commit SHA dotfiles_profile personal personal or work; independent of package selection dotfiles_home /home/ubuntu Guest account boundary; the role rejects another home dotfiles_checkout /home/ubuntu/.local/share/dotfiles/source User-owned source, never root's personal configuration

The role requires the new --check and --package-set interfaces from the selected commit and always selects the lightweight homelab package set. It does not invoke a full workstation package installer on every run. Ansible owns APT convergence; dotfiles owns the package names, plugins, configuration, backup/restore, and official kubectl version/checksums.

kubectl is downloaded directly from dl.k8s.io, verified by SHA-256, and checked against its declared version. The selected client must be within one Kubernetes minor of K3s. An existing unrelated user-local binary is preserved and causes a clear failure rather than a silent replacement. Updating the pin may require an explicit, backed-up binary migration.

Configuration and plugin checks return 0 when current, 3 when changes are needed, and another nonzero status on errors. Ansible installs only missing plugins and deploys configuration only after a real content difference. An unchanged second run creates no new configuration backups. Full live acceptance remains required.

docs.title: Monitoring Budget
docs.text:
Component CPU request Memory request / limit Persistent storage Prometheus 250m 768 MiB / 2 GiB 12 GiB; 3 days or 8 GB retention Grafana 100m 128 MiB / 512 MiB 2 GiB Alertmanager 25m 64 MiB / 256 MiB 1 GiB Operator 100m 128 MiB / 256 MiB None kube-state-metrics 50m 64 MiB / 256 MiB None Node exporter, per node 25m 32 MiB / 128 MiB None

Grafana sidecars and chart jobs add small extra requests. The storage class is homelab-retained unless the non-secret Ansible variable monitoring_storage_class selects an existing class. This does not install NFS, CSI, external storage, or backups for you.

See provisioning, operations, and monitoring access.

docs.title: Public Repository Security
docs.text: The public repository contains desired configuration, public examples, non-secret version/checksum pins, and tests. Your controller and Ubuntu KVM host remain the trust boundary; GitHub Actions never deploys infrastructure.

docs.title: Credentials and State
docs.text:
Material Storage Rule SSH private key SSH agent or private key store outside Git Never generated by Terraform SSH public key Ignored local tfvars; passed to cloud-init Public, but keep personal key metadata out of examples K3s, Grafana, and Authelia credentials Encrypted .local/vault.yml Preserve originals for recovery Vault password Private .local/vault-password, mode 0600 Move recovery copy to a password manager; never commit TLS CA and server private keys Private .local/pki, files mode 0600 No automatic Mac trust-store installation Kubeconfig .local/kubeconfig, mode 0600 Cluster-administrator credential Terraform state and saved plans Ignored local files or a private locked backend Treat all state and plans as sensitive Idempotence reports .local/idempotence.json, mode 0600 May include operational metadata; never CI artifacts etcd snapshots and VM backups Encrypted off-host storage Contain credentials and application data

sensitive = true is output redaction, not encryption. This repository avoids Terraform password/private-key resources and Kubernetes/Helm providers so those credentials never enter its state. Libvirt uses the existing SSH identity rather than a new API credential. State still reveals network topology and infrastructure metadata and must be protected.

For one operator, an encrypted workstation disk and encrypted off-host state backup are the default. For collaboration, use a private remote backend with encryption, versioning, and locking. Configure backend authentication outside Git and migrate existing state deliberately with terraform init -migrate-state. Never run concurrent operators against independent copies of local state.

Ansible secret tasks use no_log, suppress diffs, avoid cached token facts, and keep token/config files root-only. No plaintext vault file is created by the generation helper. Decrypting or editing a vault is a separate trusted operator action; your editor and workstation must also be protected.

docs.title: Network Policy at the VM Boundary
docs.text:
The guests use a dedicated nftables input table with default drop. It does not flush Kubernetes/CNI tables or add a competing forwarding policy:

Source Destination Allowed PN51 NAT gateway Guests TCP 22, 80, 443, 6443 for SSH/tunnels and ingress proxy Private node subnet Nodes UDP 8472; TCP 80, 443, 6443, 10250 Pod subnet API and kubelet TCP 6443, 10250 Guest outbound Package/image registries, DNS, time, other destinations Allowed; replies are statefully tracked

Flannel VXLAN is not encrypted. Keep this LAN/VLAN trusted and do not expose UDP 8472 to the internet. VM firewalls do not isolate pods from one another: application namespaces still need appropriate Kubernetes NetworkPolicies and RBAC. This baseline intentionally does not claim a zero-trust pod network.

No broad NodePort range, host metrics port, RDP, or VNC network service is opened. K3s includes Traefik and ServiceLB inside the private VMs. The API is accessed through a loopback-only SSH tunnel; services remain ClusterIP behind ingress. After guarded cutover, the host proxy accepts only 192.168.1.0/24 on 80/443. Both proxy ACLs and UFW define this boundary.

Guest UFW is not configured by this workflow. Do not apply an old generic UFW or hardening script over the cluster: forwarding rules and strict reverse-path filtering can break the CNI. Platform namespace policies restrict ingress and egress; monitoring admits only its own workloads, Traefik, and authorized API health probes. Authelia defaults to deny and requires MFA on every dashboard.

docs.title: Host and Cluster Privileges
docs.text:
The cloud-init ubuntu account has passwordless sudo, because Ansible must configure the guests without embedding sudo credentials. Treat its SSH key as a guest-root credential. Root SSH and password SSH are disabled. The PN51 host uses terminal-authenticated sudo, not passwordless host sudo. Membership in system libvirt is privileged and is granted only to the existing administrator.

K3s enables Secret encryption at rest and protects kubeconfig/token permissions. Workers join with the running server's CA-pinned secure token, not only a short bootstrap password. Existing token mismatch and stale worker identity checks fail closed. Token rotation and etcd restores are deliberate operations, not automatic convergence.

The monitoring namespace permits privileged pod security because node-exporter needs host inspection. Do not allow untrusted workloads or namespace-admin users there. Keep application namespaces restricted separately. Grafana Secret values are outside Helm release values, but remain Kubernetes Secrets: base64 is not encryption and cluster administrators can read them. Platform pods are restricted, non-root, and use read-only root filesystems. Headlamp has no cluster-admin binding or persistent bearer-token Secret; operators mint short-lived read-only tokens. TLS private keys and vault secrets are reconciled without logging them.

Homepage has no Kubernetes token or Docker socket and accepts only its declared ingress hostname. Argo CD is isolated in its own restricted namespace and is a trusted, privileged controller. Its external UI requires Authelia MFA plus Argo CD login; anonymous access is disabled. The locked default project and the repository/namespace-scoped homelab project prevent accidental infrastructure adoption. Do not grant untrusted users project administration or access to repository credentials. No Application or auto-sync is created by bootstrap.

docs.title: How to Check Before Publishing
docs.text:
git status --short
git check-ignore pn51/terraform/terraform.tfvars .local/vault.yml .local/kubeconfig
make secrets-scan

Review staged files and diffs before committing. The working-tree secret scan uses Git's tracked and nonignored file list, so it includes new public source without scanning private runtime data. A direct gitleaks dir can also flag legitimate credentials in ignored private directories on an operator's machine. Never upload raw output or solve that by committing those directories or globally disabling rules. No path-based scanner exception is added to hide tracked secrets.

Git ignore rules do not protect a file that was already committed. Remove the file from tracking, rotate the exposed credential immediately, then coordinate history cleanup as needed. Deleting the latest file does not remove it from Git history or forks. The existing application Secret example has empty values; populate real application secrets through a separate secret-management workflow.

docs.title: How to Rotate Secrets
docs.text:
Rotate SSH keys by adding and testing a new public key before removing the old one; cloud-init is first-boot configuration, so existing guests may need an explicit authorized-keys update or rebuild.

K3s server-token rotation changes datastore bootstrap protection: follow the K3s token procedure, update the encrypted vault and root token files deliberately, and take a new snapshot. Preserve old tokens with snapshots that require them. The role deliberately refuses an unexplained token change on an existing node.

Grafana reads its initial admin password into its persistent database. Rotating only the Kubernetes Secret does not change that database password. Use Grafana's documented account-administration flow, update the vault, and verify login. Never put a new password in a CLI argument that will be logged.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Trust failures require correct CAs or verified host fingerprints, not insecure flags. Unexpected secret-scan findings require a local review with redacted output. Restore failures involving tokens require the snapshot's original token, not an attempt to brute-force a fresh credential into the datastore.

See provisioning, operations, and testing.

docs.title: Testing and Acceptance
docs.text: There are two different claims to verify: the source describes a coherent lab, and that lab actually converges on your PN51. CI proves the first. Only live acceptance and recovery exercises can prove the second.

docs.title: Credential-Free Gates
docs.text:
make setup
make check

The chart download and dependency installation require internet access, but no host, guest SSH, vault, or Kubernetes credentials. Tests never call Terraform apply against the host.

Gate Evidence Terraform fmt/validate Configuration matches the pinned real provider schema Terraform mocked plans Exactly four VMs; one server/three workers; RAM budget; NAT; cloud-init; separate retained disks; deterministic inventory Negative Terraform cases Small/excessive RAM, gateway/IP collisions, overlapping networks, private-key input, bad image digest rejected Ansible production lint Fully qualified modules, schema/syntax, task conventions, YAML formatting Real Ansible templates All four host configs rendered; server/agent flag separation; token-file use; unchanged second render Platform render gate 33 real resources; seven MFA/TLS routes, restricted containers, credential-free Homepage, network policies, read-only Headlamp RBAC Argo CD chart gate Exact official archive checksum, three CRDs, private services, non-root workloads, disabled anonymous access, repository/namespace project limits Python regressions Private modes, symlinks, vault encryption/failure, inventory precedence, replacement scope and PV guards, idempotence evidence Dotfiles role contracts Mutable revisions rejected before package installation; public source and ubuntu ownership; local configuration fixture changes only when necessary Real pinned chart Exact archive checksum; strict Helm lint; render against pinned Kubernetes version; private services; persistent storage; existing Grafana Secret CRD regression All ten real CRDs parse safely; YAML = scalar handled without Python-object construction MkDocs strict Navigation and local documentation links build without warnings Secret scanning Redacted Git-history scan in CI; tracked and nonignored working files scanned before publication

The GitHub workflow pins its actions to commit IDs, uses a frozen Python lockfile, and grants infrastructure validation read-only repository access. It has no homelab credentials or self-hosted runner. Documentation publishing has its own separate write-capable workflow.

docs.title: How to Run Live Acceptance
docs.text:
After initial configuration:

make verify

This requires the private inventory/kubeconfig and a reachable cluster. It checks all declared node names, exact K3s versions and Ready conditions, monitoring Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet replica health, retained Bound application claims, Grafana database health, healthy Prometheus targets, Authelia/Headlamp/Homepage, Argo CD workload and server health, live project restrictions, DNS, Traefik, metrics, local-path storage, and helm test. Helm test creates a temporary chart test pod; it does not rebuild VMs.

Also verify host and VM boot behavior, guest input firewall rules, and that a non-admin machine cannot reach guest SSH or the server API. After cutover, test HTTPS certificate validation, Authelia MFA, and denied anonymous dashboard access. An internal health check does not prove the external access boundary.

docs.title: How to Prove Full Convergence
docs.text:
make idempotence

The first run establishes desired state. The second full run writes a private JSON callback report and must show zero changes, failures, unreachable hosts, rescued tasks, and ignored failures on the exact four expected hosts. An empty report, missing host, or partial --limit run cannot pass the evidence checker.

The report stays under ignored .local/; do not upload it as a public artifact. When dotfiles is enabled, run make idempotence CONFIG_FILE=.local/config.yml. The role checks package state, missing plugins, and managed configuration separately; it does not hide a full bootstrap behind an always-unchanged command. If a task changes again, inspect that exact task rather than hiding it with a blanket changed_when: false. Pure observation commands are intentionally unchanged; actual package, Secret, file, service, and Helm changes are not hidden.

docs.title: How to Exercise Recovery
docs.text: On an isolated test copy, prove that a stateless worker can be replaced and rejoin under its original name, that protected data survives root replacement, that unprotected local data is refused, and that etcd plus application data can be restored from off-host backups. Run live acceptance and idempotence after each exercise. Never test a production restore against conflicting libvirt names or addresses.

docs.title: Verification Limits
docs.text:
Mocked plans do not prove libvirt permissions, image boot behavior, guest-agent startup, protected filesystem mounting, CNI traffic, kernel compatibility, or physical capacity. Chart rendering does not prove successful operator scheduling or database migration. Local template convergence is not a substitute for the full live second-run check.

The repository deliberately does not claim those live results until you run the gates on your host. Known controller collection deprecation warnings are not suppressed globally; review them when updating pinned dependencies.

The sibling dotfiles project has independent offline and real-plugin tests for MacBook personal/work profiles. Its Ubuntu 26.04 CI covers both the workstation and lightweight homelab package sets. With Docker running, use DOTFILES_PACKAGE_SET=homelab make ubuntu there to test the lightweight native installer. A passing local Ansible fixture does not prove the full VM deployment or replace those native Linux checks.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Run the failing slice directly with make lint, make chart-check, make test-templates, or uv run --frozen python -m pytest. Use terraform -chdir=pn51/terraform test for mocked plans. For a live failure, inspect node/pod events and the exact failing Ansible task without enabling secret-bearing debug output.

See operations, reference, and monitoring troubleshooting.

docs.title: Asus PN51
docs.text: Component Target CPU AMD Ryzen 7 5700U, 8 cores / 16 threads Graphics Integrated Radeon for the Desktop host; no guest GPU passthrough Network Existing Wi-Fi at 192.168.1.20; guest NAT does not replace the LAN interface Memory 32 GiB Storage 1 TB NVMe Hypervisor Ansible-managed KVM/libvirt on Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 LTS

docs.title: Resource Budget
docs.text:
Guest Role vCPU RAM Disk pn51-server-1 K3s control plane and embedded etcd 2 4 GiB 64 GiB root + 64 GiB retained pn51-worker-1 K3s worker 2 4 GiB 64 GiB root + 64 GiB retained pn51-worker-2 K3s worker 2 4 GiB 64 GiB root + 64 GiB retained pn51-worker-3 K3s worker 2 4 GiB 64 GiB root + 64 GiB retained

Ubuntu Desktop stays on the physical host. Guests run Ubuntu Server from a checksummed cloud image with cloud-init networking, keys, and guest-agent bootstrap. No guest GUI or interactive ISO installation is needed.

Administration uses verified SSH through the PN51 jump host and a loopback-only API tunnel. Guest password/root SSH remain disabled. Separate protected data disks survive worker root replacement; off-host backups are still required.

The control plane is tainted to keep ordinary workloads on workers. Monitoring, Authelia, and Headlamp have bounded resource requests. The default leaves about half the host memory for Ubuntu Desktop and the hypervisor.

See architecture, provisioning, and configuration reference.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Git[Public Git repository] --> CI[Credential-free validation]
    Git --> Controller[Trusted administrator workstation]
    Controller -->|Ansible: host reconciliation| Host[Ubuntu Desktop and KVM on PN51]
    Controller -->|Terraform: SSH and system libvirt| Host
    Host -->|Cloud-init: key and private address| Guests[Four Ubuntu Server 26.04 VMs]
    Controller -->|Ansible: verified SSH| Guests
    Guests --> Baseline[Server baseline and protected data disks]
    Guests --> Cluster[K3s: one server and three workers]
    Controller -->|Helm through verified Kubernetes API| Monitoring[Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager]
    Cluster --> Monitoring
    Cluster --> Platform[Traefik, Authelia MFA, Headlamp, Homepage]
    Controller -->|Pinned Helm bootstrap| Argo[Argo CD]
    Argo -->|Reviewed repository and application namespace only| Apps[Application workloads]

GitHub Actions validates source and scans Git history. It cannot reach the homelab and receives no SSH key, vault password, or kubeconfig. The separate documentation publisher only writes the documentation branch.

Terraform owns VM identity, CPU, RAM, replaceable root disks, protected data disks, the NAT network, addresses, and imported image. Cloud-init owns the initial ubuntu account and authorized public keys. Ansible waits for cloud-init to finish, then owns the Ubuntu host, guest baseline/firewall, K3s, monitoring, platform, and Argo CD bootstrap. Argo CD owns only explicitly admitted application workloads; its default project is locked and it does not adopt Ansible-managed resources. Legacy retirement is a separately guarded cold-backup and ingress cutover.

The private Ansible inventory comes from Terraform output. CIDRs and the cluster DNS address travel through that inventory rather than being duplicated in group variables. Helm release credentials are not stored in Terraform state.

docs.title: Physical and Logical Topology
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Admin[Mac controller and trusted LAN] -->|SSH and LAN HTTPS| Host
    subgraph PN51[PN51: one physical failure domain]
        Host[Ubuntu Desktop and KVM: about half RAM reserved]
        Host --> Bridge[virbr51: private NAT 10.51.0.0/24]
        Bridge --> Server[server-1: K3s and single-member etcd]
        Bridge --> Worker1[worker-1: K3s agent]
        Bridge --> Worker2[worker-2: K3s agent]
        Bridge --> Worker3[worker-3: K3s agent]
        Server <-->|6443, 10250, UDP 8472| Worker1
        Server <-->|6443, 10250, UDP 8472| Worker2
        Server <-->|6443, 10250, UDP 8472| Worker3
        Worker1 --- LocalStorage[Separate protected data disks]
        Worker2 --- LocalStorage
        Worker3 --- LocalStorage
    end
    LocalStorage --> OffHost[Operator-managed off-host backups]
    Server --> OffHost

All node pairs also exchange VXLAN and kubelet traffic where required. The diagram abbreviates those links. No etcd ports or NodePort range are exposed between VMs: this is not a multi-server etcd cluster, and applications are not published directly. The dedicated host proxy forwards LAN 80/443 to Traefik; Authelia protects the dashboard routes, while the API uses the SSH tunnel.

docs.title: Why These Choices
docs.text:
Decision Reason Cost Native Ubuntu KVM/libvirt Keeps the existing Desktop host and automates VM lifecycle Host libvirt access is privileged Server guests Smaller memory, disk, and attack surface; Desktop is only a host requirement No guest graphical desktop Cloud image, cloud-init, Ansible Checksummed base and repeatable bootstrap without interactive installers First boot needs package/DNS access K3s rather than kubeadm Bundled runtime, CNI, storage bootstrap, and lower operational overhead K3s-specific configuration and upgrade procedures One server and three workers Leaves three workload nodes and a simple recovery model API outage on server restart; no control-plane HA Embedded etcd Native scheduled snapshots and a documented restore path One member is not redundant storage Scoped nftables input firewall Default-deny guest ingress without flushing CNI state Forwarding and pod isolation need their own controls Protected data disks and retained local-path storage Root replacement preserves application files Node affinity remains; not replicated or protected against NVMe failure Traefik and Authelia HTTPS plus default-deny MFA for dashboards Internal CA trust and enrollment remain explicit Read-only Headlamp Inspect Kubernetes with short-lived tokens Mutating administrator UI access is not granted by default Vault and existing SSH keys No credential generation or Kubernetes authentication in Terraform Vault password and backups remain operator responsibilities

Three control-plane VMs on this same host would tolerate a guest failure, but not a PN51 power, network, or disk failure. For useful HA, add independent physical hosts and storage before increasing control-plane count.

docs.title: Reconciliation and Recovery
docs.text:
Normal configuration runs do not perform unconditional package upgrades, reboot nodes, rotate credentials, or restart SSH/K3s. Templates and checksums notify handlers only when their inputs change. Workers are updated serially and drained before K3s changes; disruption budgets are respected.

Worker replacement is intentionally separate from reconciliation. Its helper checks node-local volumes, checks the remaining nodes, validates the complete Terraform plan, and asks for an exact typed confirmation. Control-plane replacement requires snapshot recovery.

The design is declarative at its ownership boundaries, not a promise that state can be thrown away. Preserve the Terraform state, vault, original server token, etcd snapshots, and application backups outside the PN51.

See the input reference and security boundaries.

docs.title: Guest Baseline
docs.text: The Ansible baseline role is the only supported guest-bootstrap path. Do not run the former one-off hardening scripts over these nodes; their UFW, reverse-path filtering, package-upgrade, and service behavior conflict with this design.

docs.title: Enforced State
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 26.04 x86-64 guest and minimum-memory assertions, after cloud-init.
  • Lean server packages, OpenSSH, AppArmor, guest agent, and security updates.
  • Public-key SSH only, no root SSH, low authentication-attempt limit, early drop-in precedence, and configuration validation before a conditional reload.
  • Root-only K3s config/token and administrator kubeconfig; no token in systemd arguments or Terraform state.
  • Persisted bridge-netfilter/overlay modules, forwarding enabled, and CNI-safe reverse-path filtering. Kubernetes kernel-protection defaults are explicit.
  • Swap removed from active state and fstab; sleep/suspend targets masked.
  • Security updates enabled without automatic reboots.
  • Server boot target and a separate protected ext4 data disk; existing signatures are checked before a blank disk is formatted.

VM ingress uses a dedicated default-drop nftables input table, not guest UFW or a flush of Kubernetes forwarding tables. Retained storage and etcd snapshots use the data disk. Validate network boundaries from another machine. AppArmor remains enabled; this is not a CIS certification claim.

docs.title: How to Verify the Baseline
docs.text:
Run make configure, inspect the guest services and data mounts, then run make verify and make idempotence. On each guest, inspect SSH's effective configuration with sudo sshd -T, swap with swapon --show, and the boot target with systemctl get-default.

If networking fails, inspect the owned nftables rules, kernel settings, CNI pods, and routes before adding broad allow rules. If SSH hardening fails validation, keep the existing verified connection open and repair the failing setting.

See security boundaries, testing, and maintenance.

docs.title: Threat Model
docs.text: This lab assumes a trusted administrator workstation, a private trusted node network, a patched Ubuntu KVM host, and Ubuntu/GitHub/Helm artifacts obtained through verified TLS and pinned checksums where supported.

docs.title: What the Baseline Addresses
docs.text: Risk Control Public Git credential exposure Ignored local artifacts, Vault, no private-key generation in Terraform, history scans Accidental network exposure Default-drop VM input, private NAT, LAN proxy ACLs, MFA-protected dashboards Man-in-the-middle administration Verified host/guest SSH keys, Kubernetes CA validation, internal HTTPS, secure worker join Configuration drift Declarative roles, handlers, mock/template tests, full live second-run acceptance Unintended destructive replacement Exact worker selection, PV guard, full-plan scope validation, typed confirmation Accidental cluster identity loss Stable inventory, stale-node detection, token mismatch guard, documented restore requirements

docs.title: What Remains an Operator Responsibility
docs.text:
One machine cannot provide physical high availability. Its NVMe disk and local volumes are not replicated. Scheduled local etcd snapshots are not off-host backups. A compromised administrator key, Ubuntu KVM host, or cluster-admin kubeconfig can control the lab.

Desktop remains only on the physical host. Node-exporter needs host inspection; its namespace permits privileged pod security. VXLAN traffic is private-network traffic, not an encrypted overlay. The cluster does not claim universal default-deny policy for arbitrary future workloads. The platform namespace has explicit network restrictions and the declared dashboards require Authelia MFA; new application namespaces need their own policies.

Do not publish workloads until you have designed namespace RBAC, appropriate NetworkPolicies, ingress TLS/authentication, dependency updates, and application backup/restore. PodSecurityPolicy is removed from modern Kubernetes; use Pod Security Admission and current policy tooling instead.

See the enforced guest baseline, secret and network controls, and backup/restore procedures.
